query: Earlier automotive-catalyst research reported that Cu–Ni catalysts can oxidize CO and hydrocarbons at lower temperatures without platinum-group metals, while Pd–Cu and Pt–Cu catalysts can resist poisoning by H2O and NO and enable oxidation below 150 °C. Multi-principal-element catalysts in nearly equiatomic ratios have also been explored as a framework for combining high activity, thermal stability, and reduced platinum-group-metal use. These prior results demonstrate individual capabilities but do not establish the combined performance demanded by increasingly stringent regulations: clean exhaust during transient and low-temperature operation, resistance to relevant poisons, and durability over a vehicle lifetime despite the mileage-related degradation observed in real-driving-emission studies. Starting from a near-equiatomic, multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst, what single intervention could address this combined activity, poisoning-resistance, and lifetime-durability problem without sacrificing low platinum-group-metal use? State one hypothesis identifying the intervention, explaining how it would work, predicting the change relative to the unmodified catalyst, defining the exhaust and aging conditions over which it should apply, citing supporting prior evidence, and specifying an experiment whose result would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: An inverse-model-guided synthesis intervention that uses high-alkalinity and low-temperature continuous-solvothermal processing to steer the multi-element alloy catalyst towards a beneficial Cu–Pt enriched surface configuration will simultaneously improve low-temperature oxidation activity, poisoning-resistance, and durability after severe ageing.
generation.material_initial_state: Fresh 1 wt% multi-element alloy catalyst candidates prepared from up to 19 metal precursors and deposited on La-doped γ-Al2O3, with agglomerates of fine metallic particles and without prior accelerated thermal ageing.
generation.intervention: Employing a closed-loop, high-throughput discovery method with automated continuous-solvothermal synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning prediction and Bayesian optimization to select synthesis parameters (200–350 °C, high alkalinity with 25 M NaOH, and controlled pressure) that favor a Cu–Pt surface rearrangement.
generation.conditions: Ageing performed at 900 °C for 5 h under cyclic lean/rich conditions in a water-containing, near-stoichiometric feed (500 ppm NO, 5000 ppm CO, 200 ppm C3H6, 120 ppm i-C5H12, 14% CO2, 4900 ppm O2, 1700 ppm H2 and balance N2) followed by testing from 100 to 500 °C at a 10 °C min−1 ramp.
generation.structural_mediator: Post-ageing electronic and atomic reconstruction that promotes the formation of electronically coupled Cu–Pt cooperative adsorption sites along with beneficial alloy/support interfacial states, while limiting detrimental phase segregation or excessive incorporation of Fe/Ni/Cu into the La–Al mixed oxides.
generation.mechanism: During the controlled synthesis and subsequent ageing, the Cu–Pt surface rearrangement is expected to create cooperative sites that modulate CO adsorption (by weakening excessively strong binding) and improve redox buffering and oxygen mobility, thereby coupling efficient hydrocarbon oxidation with NO reduction. This avoids the electronic isolation of Pt often caused by its coordination with Ni/Fe, ultimately lowering the light-off temperature and enhancing overall conversion.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to a Pd/Al2O3 baseline catalyst and catalysts obtained via random synthesis parameters, the targeted formulation is predicted to achieve at least a 5 °C lower T50 (temperature at which 50% conversion is attained) and a minimum improvement of 2 percentage points in conversion at 350 °C after severe ageing.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics established by a Pd/Al2O3 benchmark tested under identical cyclic ageing and reaction conditions, as well as performance from randomly selected multi-element catalyst compositions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies within the explored five- to nineteen-element, 1 wt% supported catalyst space, under accelerated ageing at 900 °C for 5 h in a near-stoichiometric exhaust environment (containing NO, CO, C3H6, and i-C5H12). Detailed structure–performance correlations are based on ex situ characterizations and may not translate quantitatively outside these conditions.
generation.uncertainty: While the intervention is expected to favor beneficial Cu–Pt interactions, the precise quantitative impact may vary with the detailed synthesis conditions and operating environment. The causal link between nanoscale segregation and catalytic activity has inherent uncertainties due to variability in local alloying and support effects.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform automated light-off measurements and species-resolved conversion assessments for NO, CO, C3H6, and i-C5H12 on both the tailored catalysts and the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark after severe ageing. Complement this with fresh versus aged CO-adsorption FT-IR studies to track changes in adsorption sites, and HAADF-STEM/EDS analyses to verify particle morphology and elemental distributions. Compare the hit rate and quantitative performance improvements (T50 and conversion at 350 °C) between catalysts obtained via the inverse-model-guided synthesis and those from random selections.
measurements: T50 and species-specific conversion curves (NO, CO, C3H6, i-C5H12) from light-off tests
CO-adsorption FT-IR spectra indicating changes in electronic coupling and adsorption sites
HAADF-STEM/EDS imaging for particle morphology and elemental mapping
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the inverse-model-guided catalysts do not exhibit a measurable improvement of at least a 5 °C decrease in T50 or a 2 percentage-point improvement in conversion at 350 °C relative to the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark (or if no evident Cu–Pt surface enrichment is observed by spectroscopic and microscopic analyses), the hypothesis should be rejected.
